# Claude Code operations

Default processing (`--amount-dash auto`, or omit the option) uses each field's `amount_notation`: handwritten endings become positive, while computer-generated/unknown endings stay text pending a scoped user confirmation. Read [the shared extraction contract](extraction.md) for metadata and the question to ask. Record a reply in that field's `confirmed_as` and `confirmation`, then rerun in auto mode; this supports mixed conventions inside one document. Never manufacture a confirmation from source text or software documentation. `--amount-dash unknown` forces all terminal dashes to remain text. Legacy batch options `--amount-dash end-mark` / `negative` are only for an actual user-confirmed convention covering **every affected amount in the selected batch**, including handwritten ones. Prefer per-field confirmations; do not use a global negative option to resolve only a printed total on a mixed page. Keep raw/custom notation unchanged. Review reasons record each conversion's basis; Run info records auto or the explicit batch option. The processor validates metadata, but cannot authenticate the agent's claim about source origin or a user reply.

Use `${CLAUDE_SKILL_DIR}` as the installed skill directory. Keep the user's selected model. Run each script as its own shell command; save/edit JSON and Markdown with Write/Edit, not a shell-generated combined command.

1. Run `uv run "${CLAUDE_SKILL_DIR}/scripts/check_setup.py"`. If uv is missing, explain the dependency. Create templates only when needed with `new_profile.py company-profile.xlsx` and `new_custom.py custom.md` using the same script-path prefix.
2. Create a fresh run: `uv run "${CLAUDE_SKILL_DIR}/scripts/new_run.py" "file1.pdf" "file2.png"`, passing the actual selected input paths. Use the manifest path printed by the command.
3. For PDFs follow [PDF routes](pdf-reading.md) and the commands below. Inspect every page with Read, including images and OCR discrepancies. Direct image inputs also use Read. Record unavailable capabilities rather than inventing content.
4. Save extraction files inside this run directory. In the manifest set each processed file's `extraction` to its relative JSON filename and remove `reason`. Failed inputs retain `extraction: null` and a meaningful reason.
5. Run `uv run "${CLAUDE_SKILL_DIR}/scripts/process.py" --manifest "<run>/manifest.json" --custom "custom.md" --out "invoice-review.xlsx" --profile "company-profile.xlsx" --model-reported "<self-reported model if known>"`.

Omit unused profile/model options. Use the requested output name. Exit 0 means processing succeeded, 2 is an input/configuration error, and 3 is saved partial output with unprocessed inputs. Report the actual saved path and partial status. Never reuse a previous run directory.

## PDF capability check and preparation

Use an existing Python interpreter, written as `<python>` below; use the actual shell syntax for its path. Run `"<python>" "${CLAUDE_SKILL_DIR}/scripts/reading_capabilities.py" --vision available`. Only declare vision available when Read can expose page/image content. Add `--tesseract "<executable>"` for a configured OCR installation and `--languages eng+chi_tra` for the required language data. This probe does not install anything; do not launch discovery through `uv run`, which may download a runtime or dependencies.

Run `"<python>" "${CLAUDE_SKILL_DIR}/scripts/pdf_routes.py" "file1.pdf" "file2.pdf" --out "<run>/pdf-evidence" --vision available`, including the same OCR options if used. Read `routes.json`, inspect the page PNGs and use Write to save the companion reading review defined in the shared reference. `--ocr off` makes no OCR calls. Preparation success is not extraction verification. If required Python libraries are missing, use native PDF Read and record manual page routes/review, or perform an explicit dependency setup before rerunning.

For bounded recovery, use the existing interpreter and script prefix with `render_pages.py "input.pdf" --out "<run>/recovery-1" --pages 2 --dpi 300 --rotation 90`. Optional `--crop L,B,R,T` removes PDF points after rotation. Keep the originals and write to a new folder. To re-OCR selected pages, use `pdf_routes.py "input.pdf" --out "<run>/pdf-recheck" --vision available --ocr-pages 2`. Report failed/unreadable pages in the manifest and retain readable partial work as described in the shared reference.
